scope: Equal-depth verification for a library/lagoon cultural edge, a financial-district pedestrian/transit section, and a contemporary museum whose galleries, terrace, park and water mirrors form one civic system.

sources.supports: Weekly 2026 reading-club meetings occur at Centro Cultural El Olivar and neighborhood centers, corroborating active library-linked communal reading.
May 2026 permanent cleaning/conservation work on the central lagoon and its biodiversity establishes current maintained ecological infrastructure.
February 2026 maintenance covered lagoon benches, bridge and posts; the Olivar has more than 1,600 olive trees and functions as community landscape.

sources.publisher: Autoridad de Transporte Urbano para Lima y Callao
sources.supports: May 2026 inspection confirms completed vestibule expansion and Andrés Reyes station addition supporting Canaval y Moreyra capacity; wider modernization remains under evaluation.

sources.publisher: Autoridad de Transporte Urbano para Lima y Callao
sources.supports: February 2026 ATU plan identifies Canaval y Moreyra as a key peak station receiving additional intermediate boarding infrastructure; implementation state requires field confirmation.
Six free municipal electric buses operate through financial-zone routes in 2026, adding current inclusive mobility to worker/visitor flows.
Institution describes three industrial-type gallery volumes, terrace, park and cultural/public program as an integrated museum setting.
May 2026 program documents mediation, collective mural, workshops and extended occupation; the event is completed and some activities required registration.
National guide identifies MAC as an open-to-all private cultural institution on 14,651 m² municipal-concession land with published museum hours; hours require current recheck.

contradictions: Current library/cultural activity and lagoon maintenance are verified separately, but no source proves that readers routinely occupy the lagoon sightline in one frame.
The picturesque reflection view can obscure the library's cultural role and reduce maintained ecological infrastructure to scenery.
Weekly reading-club activity proves program continuity but not a specific outdoor session or route window.
composition_questions: Can ramp/doorway, lagoon edge and a real reading or maintenance verb show culture and ecology as one public system rather than a reflection postcard?
Which foliage, water glare, parked vehicle, bird cluster or façade crop severs the library from the maintained lagoon edge?
Does moving from the obvious waterside view to the ramp/bridge tangent reveal exchange between indoor reading and outdoor community life, or is the relation only geographic?

source_truth.answer: The active Centro Cultural/Biblioteca Municipal sits within the maintained El Olivar landscape near its central lagoon, which receives permanent conservation work in 2026.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Library/cultural rooms, accessible approach, bridge, benches, lagoon and historic grove distribute indoor learning and outdoor pause through a civic-natural edge.

current_life.answer: Weekly reading dialogue, library use, walking, sitting, ecological maintenance and wildlife observation are current, but their same-frame overlap must be field-proven.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Read, meet, enter, cross, sit, clean, observe and pause are evidenced. An empty maintained bridge/bench between program waves can express public expectation.

architectural_causality.answer: Ramp, steps, bridge, benches, water edge and tree canopy stage transitions between cultural enclosure and shared ecological landscape.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Quiet façade and lagoon reflection dominate. The underused relation is an accessible cultural threshold visibly linked to reading, crossing or lagoon care.

light_material_geometry.answer: Filtered light and garúa can join white façade, ramp, water and olive trunks; reflection, birds or foliage alone cannot carry architectural causality.

position_then_optics.answer: Test library-ramp-to-lagoon, bridge-to-entry and water-edge reverse views. Start 35 mm for system, 50 mm for reader/crossing and 85 mm only if threshold and lagoon remain connected.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Confirm library/event access, remain off planted/water edges, avoid identifiable children and nesting wildlife disturbance, and never stage a reader outdoors.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: Passes when library threshold and maintained landscape visibly cause a current cultural/ecological verb. A reflection postcard or generic reader fails.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Public bridge/path tangent aligning lagoon edge, accessible ramp and library entrance

B_HABITAR.position: Public approach where consenting adult reader exits toward bridge/bench
B_HABITAR.expected_action: Adult exits, pauses and turns toward landscape

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Library-side ramp looking through bridge/lagoon rather than across reflection
C_ANTI_POSTAL.edge_guards: No centered reflection or bird spectacle

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: Public oblique compressing ramp rail, water edge, olive trunks and façade
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.expected_action: Shadow or cleaner/walker trace crosses layers

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Public diagonal joining library arrival, bridge/bench and maintained lagoon
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.expected_action: Entering, reading/pausing and crossing occupy three zones

contradictions: Completed Canaval y Moreyra/Andrés Reyes capacity works are verified, while planned intermediate boarding and broader modernization may still be incomplete.
Municipal electric buses traverse the financial zone but no source proves a repeatable transfer at the selected station edge.
Historic pedestrian-space recovery and academic comfort deficits predate 2026; current sidewalk quality and exact intervention footprint require field revalidation.
composition_questions: Can expanded station access, expressway trench and office-street flow visibly convert tower-district workers into multimodal pedestrians rather than a skyline crowd?
Which railing, vehicle, vendor, advertising panel, construction barrier or tower reflection destroys the station-to-sidewalk continuity?
Does a legal ground/bridge position reveal improved capacity alongside remaining comfort gaps, or has the current intervention invalidated the old contradiction?

source_truth.answer: The active financial district is served by expanded Canaval y Moreyra/Andrés Reyes Metropolitano infrastructure and 2026 municipal electric-bus routes amid dense office streets.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Office towers, sidewalks, expressway trench, bridges, vestibules and adjacent stations concentrate regional commuters and distribute them into the business district.

current_life.answer: Workers queue, transfer, cross, enter towers and use formal buses; additional boarding and modernization respond to continuing peak pressure but completion must be checked.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Exit, queue, climb, cross, transfer, consult, enter, deliver and wait are evidenced. A brief cleared connector can reveal designed capacity between waves.

architectural_causality.answer: Vestibules, station pair, expressway trench, bridge and office-frontage sidewalks funnel large commuter streams through limited vertical and lateral connections.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Glass-tower canyon and rush-hour crowd dominate. The underused relation is the section from trench/vestibule through bridge/sidewalk into office thresholds, including any still-visible comfort conflict.

light_material_geometry.answer: Hard sun can articulate trench, bridge and tower shadows; garúa can suppress glass spectacle, but reflection or crowd density without transfer causality fails.

position_then_optics.answer: Test legal vestibule exit, public bridge/sidewalk tangent and office-threshold reverse view. Start 35 mm for section, 50 mm for transfer gesture and 85 mm only when multiple systems remain linked.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Check works/barriers first, never block peak flows or stand in roadways, conceal cards/screens/faces, obey transit security and use lower-density edges if crowding makes photography unsafe.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: Passes when transit/public-realm architecture visibly turns office demand into a current movement hierarchy. Tower spectacle, anonymous crowd or obsolete comfort claim fails.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Legal public connector aligning trench, expanded vestibule and office-street exit
A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude ads, vehicles and clipped rails

B_HABITAR.position: Public station exit where commuter stream splits toward two office streets

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Safe sidewalk tangent linking station approach, electric-bus route and tower entry
C_ANTI_POSTAL.edge_guards: No roadway stance or bus hero shot

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: Legal oblique compressing concrete trench, rail, sidewalk and glass frontage
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.expected_action: Workers cross shadow boundaries across levels

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Legal diagonal joining station exit, sidewalk transfer and office threshold
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.expected_action: Exiting, transferring and entering occupy three zones

contradictions: The published site plan verifies two water mirrors, but their August 2026 water/maintenance condition is not established.
Noche de los Museos proves intensive occupation but is completed and partly preregistered; it is not a future route window.
Institutional sources are authoritative for program/design intent but promotional for visitor experience; ground visibility must be independently tested.
composition_questions: Can gallery volumes, terrace, water mirror and a current mediation/gathering verb read as one museum–park system rather than a reflective building portrait?
Which empty basin, fence, event furniture, glare, parked vehicle or crowd overlap breaks the threshold-to-water relationship?
Does moving to a path-level tangent reveal how the industrial volumes organize public outdoor life, or is the mirror only decorative foreground?

source_truth.answer: MAC Lima is an active contemporary-art museum composed of three industrial-type gallery volumes with terrace, park and two designed water mirrors, supporting mediation and public programs.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Gallery volumes, terrace, garden, perimeter paths and water mirrors extend exhibition encounter into an open civic landscape rather than isolating art indoors.

current_life.answer: Visitors exhibit, learn, make, gather and move between galleries and outdoor areas; exact current program, photography policy and water condition require same-day confirmation.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Enter, look, mediate, draw, assemble, cross, sit, make and disperse are evidenced. An empty terrace reflected between programs can express institutional readiness.

architectural_causality.answer: Three volumes, glazed thresholds, terrace, paths and water edges distribute visitors between contained galleries and shared outdoor cultural space.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Museum/park overview, site plan and event documentation dominate. The underused relation is a path-level visitor transition changed by the mirror/terrace geometry.

light_material_geometry.answer: Garúa can connect concrete/glass, water and lawn; low light can double occupied thresholds, but perfect reflection or empty modernism alone fails.

position_then_optics.answer: Test public park-to-terrace tangent, mirror-edge diagonal and gallery-to-landscape reverse view if permitted. Start 35 mm for system, 50 mm for mediation action and 85 mm only with threshold context.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Recheck hours, admission, event/photography rules and basin condition, remain on paths, avoid identifiable children and artworks-as-reproduction, and do not stage reflection gestures.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: Passes when museum architecture and water/park edge visibly cause current cultural encounter. Reflection postcard, art documentation or event crowd without spatial agency fails.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Public park path aligning two gallery volumes, terrace and water edge
A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude cars, glare and clipped basin
A_STRUCTURE.kill_trigger: Basin empty/blocked or only façade reads

B_HABITAR.position: Authorized/public terrace threshold beside mirror path
B_HABITAR.expected_action: Adults leave mediation activity and disperse into park

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Low path tangent along mirror toward offset gallery threshold, avoiding symmetric reflection
C_ANTI_POSTAL.expected_action: Visitor changes direction at water edge

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: Public oblique compressing concrete/glass volume, occupied threshold and partial water surface
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.light: Blue hour/internal glow or soft lateral sun

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Public/authorized diagonal joining gallery exit, terrace gathering and park/mirror circulation
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.expected_action: Exiting, gathering and crossing occupy three zones
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.edge_guards: Art and reflection subordinate to spatial use
